name: Chroma Fixes
description: Fix colour alignment, bleeding, rainbows and dot crawl
longDescription:
Repairs colour-specific damage from analog and composite video. It covers five separate problems, each with its own switch, in the order they appear below:

**Alignment** — the colour sits sideways or up/down from the picture it belongs to. Correct it automatically or by hand; these are alternatives, not a pair.

**Bleeding** — colour smears past the edge it belongs to, most obviously on strong reds.

**Dot crawl** — dots crawling along sharp colour edges.

**Rainbowing** — shimmering colour bands over fine detail.

**Chroma combing** — leftover comb teeth in the colour planes.

Dot crawl and rainbowing each offer a second removal that compares neighbouring frames rather than working inside one. They reach different patterns, so they are worth combining rather than choosing between.

Turn on only what you can actually see in the preview — every one of these costs some colour detail.

methods.name: Chroma Fixes
methods.description: Alignment, bleeding, dot crawl, rainbowing and chroma combing, each switched on separately below

ui.label: Correct colour alignment automatically
ui.description: Measures how far the colour has slipped from the picture and shifts it back, so you do not have to guess it on a slider. If it cannot measure the source reliably it leaves the picture alone rather than guessing. This replaces the manual sliders — with it on, they are not used.

ui.label: Search range
ui.description: The largest misalignment to look for, in pixels.

ui.label: Precision
ui.description: Smaller finds sub-pixel shifts, at some cost.

ui.label: Reference frame
ui.description: Measure once on this frame. -1 measures every frame, which is about 23 times slower and rarely worth it.

ui.label: Correct colour alignment by hand (Y/C delay)
ui.description: Shift the colour back into place yourself. Use this when the automatic measurement finds nothing — very soft VHS colour is sometimes not measurable.

ui.label: Horizontal shift
ui.description: Negative moves the colour left, positive moves it right, in pixels.

ui.label: Vertical shift
ui.description: Negative moves the colour up, positive moves it down, in pixels.

ui.label: Fix colour bleeding past edges
ui.description: Colour smeared beyond the edge it belongs to, most obvious on strong reds. Common on VHS and other composite captures.

ui.label: Strength
ui.description: How much of the correction to blend in.

ui.label: Colour blur
ui.description: Softens the colour before the correction. Higher hides more bleeding and loses more colour detail.

ui.label: Horizontal offset
ui.description: Whole-pixel colour offset the fix works from. Leave it alone unless the colour is misaligned as well as bleeding — the alignment controls above are the better tool for that.

ui.label: Vertical offset
ui.description: Whole-pixel colour offset the fix works from, vertically.

ui.label: Remove dot crawl
ui.description: The pattern of dots crawling along sharp colour edges on composite captures. Decided within each frame.

ui.label: Brightness threshold
ui.description: How much brightness variation still counts as dot crawl. Lower catches more.

ui.label: Colour threshold
ui.description: How much colour variation still counts as dot crawl. Lower catches more.

ui.label: Maximum change
ui.description: The most any pixel may be altered. Lower is safer on detailed pictures.

ui.label: Remove dot crawl across frames (DeDot)
ui.description: A second removal that compares neighbouring frames instead of working inside one, and skips anything that is moving. It reaches crawl patterns the one above leaves alone, so the two are worth combining. 8-bit only, so a deeper source is converted down for this step and restored after.

ui.label: Brightness (within a frame)
ui.description: How different a pixel must be from its neighbours to count as dot crawl.

ui.label: Brightness (between frames)
ui.description: How much a pixel may change between frames and still be treated as dot crawl rather than motion.

ui.label: Colour threshold
ui.description: How strongly colour is corrected.

ui.label: Colour motion limit
ui.description: Raise towards 255 to leave colour alone entirely.

ui.label: Remove rainbow shimmer
ui.description: Shimmering colour bands over fine detail on composite captures — the companion to dot crawl, which sits along edges instead. Decided within each frame.

ui.label: Colour threshold
ui.description: How different colour must be before it is treated as rainbowing. Lower catches more.

ui.label: Motion threshold
ui.description: Areas whose brightness moves more than this are left alone, which protects real motion.

ui.label: Remove rainbow shimmer across frames (Bifrost)
ui.description: Compares across frames rather than within one, so it catches rainbowing that shimmers as the picture moves. Works alongside the removal above, not instead of it. 8-bit only, so a deeper source is converted down for this step and restored after.

ui.label: Motion threshold
ui.description: Areas changing more than this between frames are treated as movement and left alone.

ui.label: Caution
ui.description: How much agreement is needed before a pixel is changed. Higher is safer and removes less.

ui.label: Remove chroma combing
ui.description: Leftover comb teeth in the colour planes, usually from a source that was deinterlaced or field-blended badly before it reached you.

ui.label: Strength
ui.description: How hard to work on the combing. Higher softens more of the picture with it.

ui.label: Maximum change
ui.description: The most any pixel may be altered. 255 places no limit.
